If you are referring to the process of dismissing somebody, then the interpretation is different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to some of the other persons you mentioned earlier. On the 1st of December, 2005, at page 19 of your interview, that is 77-78 of the B/C/S version, you once again said that: "Bosanski Samac was an area where the central authority had no control." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to say that at Samac - and now I'm talking about or from the vantage point of the analysis that was carried out - there was a renegade group and the chief of the public security station was head of it. They were acting like a criminal organisation almost. No disciplinary proceedings were initiated. We took the decision - and I'm saying "we" again, although it was me personally at that time - we decided to directly arrest Todorovic. I believe that we arrested him in the Brcko municipality and we used a special unit to do that because that was the way or the -- that we had to resort to in dealing with such persons. The conduct of the number one man was totally criminal and even the group of persons around him, they weren't even our citizens. It was basically a criminal organisation using the public security station as a storefront.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you tell us when Todorovic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I think he was arrested -- but I'm afraid I can't give you a precise answer. I remember all the elements and how we arrested him, but I'm afraid of saying something wrong if you want to hear a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can we perhaps look at tab 14, that is P406 at page 4. It says that at 9.00 a.m. on 15 November 1992, you were informed of the arrest of Todorovic by a military group. Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Can I see the following page because this is the report of the centre chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You see -- do you see your name in the -- on that page?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So can you confirm that that happened and ...

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I cannot fully confirm this because the sequence of events doesn't seem to -- I also had other information about the processing of this Steve and I believe that we met him again. This was his military arrest, but there was another arrest carried out by the police and it was during one of my terms in office, but I can't tell when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So do I understand --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: This doesn't refer to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly, Mr. Kovac, that your order to arrest him was followed by an arrest which was made by the police? Then my question would be this -- and you say this is another arrest. Can you tell us on the order of whom this other arrest had been made, if you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No, no, I can't. He was never arrested by the police except pursuant to my orders. I don't believe there was another instance. But he also had a conflict with the army. He was also arrested by the army at one point, and it's that part that ... at that time we were settling accounts with him and his activities in Samac in 1992. Bjelosevic, the centre chief, was involved on the one hand, and there was also an overlap with regard to the Samac station because the Bijeljina centre also had some jurisdiction over them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that this is how it went. We started squaring our accounts with the whole station, but the very arrest is something about which I can't really seem to make up my mind. I think that there were two, first with the army and then with us, the police, that is. The police also had some activities directed at him. But I believe you do have all this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I'm clear about the first encounter with him and his arrest by the army, but there were also some other measures of which he was the target, and I mean measures launched by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, are you saying now that the RS MUP authorities were not aware of this arrest, the military arrest, the arrest by the military?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No, no, we were aware. Of course we knew about the arrest effected by the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, let's explain this. As far as this whole process of resolving the situation in Samac is concerned. By that time we had completely -- we had -- we were completely clear about how things stood there, in Samac. It's just this section of the report about the arrest, there's some elements that somehow don't fit in, they don't seem to. But never mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I had a little trouble finding the right document, Mr. Kovac, sorry about that. Can we now turn to page 1, it should be page 1 in the B/C/S as well, where it says that you ordered an investigation into the circumstances of the arrest of Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you now turn to page 2, at the bottom. I hope it's at the bottom of the B/C/S as well. It says that: "The team that interviewed Todorovic after his arrest heard of two crimes, looting and theft of weapons." And at page 3 and 4, it describes the circumstances of general lack of discipline and control. Is -- does this document point to the reasons of Todorovic's arrest like this? Are these the reasons of Todorovic's arrest?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, amongst others, Todorovic's activity and his attitude, as well as the overall situation at the Samac public security station, and his conflicts with the army which also had detrimental consequences on the relations between the army and the MUP, clearly all these were the reasons that brought about his arrest. Only it doesn't -- it isn't presented that way in this report from the Bijeljina centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Now then can you look at tab 12A, that's 1D518. Is this the MUP decision suspending Todorovic after his arrest?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. We can see from this the request made to centre chief Bjelosevic to remove this person from his position and to appoint at the same time Savo Cancarevic and there is a reasoning. He states his reasons, namely, that Todorovic never received a decision on the appointment to these duties, but I know that the motive was that he should be removed due to the numerous illegalities in his work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But the fact that he was arrested before this decision is not mentioned in it; right? Isn't that odd?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No, it isn't odd because the manner of his arrest was not in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure. It was a result of a number of other circumstances. That was probably the reason why his arrest is not mentioned here, among others, that he was arrested and all that, formally speaking I mean. You may have noticed that the Bijeljina centre reported on his arrest and the proposal came from the chief of the Doboj centre. Andrija Bjelosevic was chief of the Doboj centre. There was some personnel reshuffling, and it's difficult for me to reconstruct who was in which position at what point in time. I know that Bjelosevic was in Doboj, though. And then he had also some activities regarding Bijeljina and then it was Doboj again. I know that in some periods Doboj was mentioned, at others Bijeljina, and Andrija Bjelosevic features as chief of the Doboj centre, but before that there is a report from the Bijeljina centre. So there was this territorial overlap, but it doesn't matter for this -- for these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Anyway, the situation was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you look then at P2 -- at tab 11, P2438.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Are you referring to this decision to appoint Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So now obviously we have the same in B/C/S and in English; right? And there it says - and that's what's troubling me a little bit, Mr. Kovac - is here it's -- the decision is that the employment of Todorovic was terminated by agreement. Have you an explanation for that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: This is a decision issued by Minister Kijac which is after my time, and what I'm looking at is a decision of Minister Adzic. And this is 1996, a year after I had left the Ministry of the Interior, and it's one year after the war. It was issued by Dragan Kijac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And you don't know about this?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It was one year later. It speaks here about consensual termination of employment, but before that there is a decision issued by Ratko Adzic in 1993 on his appointment. I'm not aware of this document dated 1996. It was not the time when I was at the ministry. It was a year after I had left. Minister Kijac was my successor and this happened one year after my departure, this consensual or termination of employment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can we have page 6 of the same document. My question here is whether you could -- whether you can explain the retroactive appointment starting 28 March 1992 issued for Stevan Todorovic as SJB chief in Samac and the decision taken on the 3rd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I can explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please do.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: This could only have been issued by an incompetent person who doesn't know anything about the law. This is totally illegal and unprofessional, and I think that for a good part it was done intentionally. This decision for Stevan Todorovic was issued by Mr. Adzic, who during his term of office annihilated and halted a lot of activities that we conducted against persons such as this one. So while he was minister, for example, in June 1993 I witnessed him issuing a retroactive decision for Stevan Todorovic on his appointment in 1992. So clearly if you look at the previous information and the proposal made by Andrija Bjelosevic for Todorovic to be removed from his position because he didn't have the letter of appointment in the first place, this was a simple cover-up. So in addition to it being an unprofessional, it is a criminal act as well. And one of the conflicts that I had with this minister was exactly because of this unprofessional conduct, because he destroyed and obliterated lots of things that we did. And this document is proof which policy he pursued because that's why he came to the ministry and not to run the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move now to the proceedings against Dragan Andan. In your interview of December 2005, page 21 and 22 in English, which are 80 -- page 80 in B/C/S, you say that the police in Bijeljina were rebelling against Andan. Can you put a time-frame to that? When were the police requesting his removal, if you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime in late August --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: -- or early September --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: -- when I came there at around 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- what it was that they were protesting against?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: They were protesting against the bad conditions and bad equipment issued to them, and they were also criticising misconduct by a number of employees who came to this area from the MUP. This included members of the federal Ministry of the Interior, and they specifically named Dragan Andan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: What was done about it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, when they were describing their difficult material situation and lack of equipment, they were pointing out the behaviour of certain employees or executives who were involved in certain activities, which would provide them with certain material gains --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, can we try to stick with Dragan Andan. What was done about this situation?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: As far as he's concerned, I said at one local meeting that I was going to institute proceedings in order to establish all the illegal activities that Dragan Andan was involved in. I initiated disciplinary proceedings and a decision, or rather, the proposals already made to suspend him pending the completion of the proceedings. The minister set up a disciplinary commission whose task was to investigate these illicit activities, or rather, allegations about the illicit activities relating to Dragan Andan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And what was the result?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: It was a standard procedure, and the result was that the minister issued a decision on temporary suspension from the MUP. The disciplinary proceedings were conducted, but I think that during the proceedings he himself left the MUP and he joined the Army of Republika Srpska. And that's what happened with Dragan Andan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you -- you say the minister issued a decision. Was it the minister or was it you yourself? Or were you the minister at the time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't minister at the time. I was assistant minister of Mico Stanisic at the time. The minister issued a decision on suspension --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: -- and he set up a commission. So that's it. So that's it, what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you look at P2349, tab 14. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Is that the decision, Mico Stanisic's decision, you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: This is a request to initiate disciplinary proceedings, and this is a document issued by Minister Stanisic, but I know that I was involved in drafting this. I was fully involved in all the preparations for this document and it was the office of Minister Stanisic who issued this and it was signed by the minister himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And was this the reasons, the reasons stated here, that -- for which he was suspended?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, these were precisely the reasons such as misappropriation of property and taking property from depots and using it for private purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we move now to Malko Koroman. I understand that you never mentioned Koroman in any of your prior interviews, but at the meeting with the Chamber's Legal Officers you confirmed that you were aware of his activities at the moment you became assistant minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I was aware of his official duty, that's what I meant. Of course when I assumed the duties of assistant minister and since one of our headquarters was at Pale, I was aware of professional career of Koroman in that period. I mainly knew the things that pertained to his professional duties and I'm referring to the period starting from August when I went to the MUP HQ. And if you wish, I can give you some details regarding some situations. Please feel free to ask me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: My next question would be: Are you aware of any measures that were taken against him for his role in the events of Pale in 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think that these activities took place prior to my arrival. Therefore, I cannot think of and I cannot remember any specific activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I wasn't involved in that at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Shall we have a look then at tab 17, which is P1461. The first question is whether you've ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't think I have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Having read part of it I can say that I wasn't aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Without going into the details, Mr. Kovac, are you aware of any proceedings initiated as a result of the complaints that are made in this document?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I can't remember any proceedings in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware whether Mr. Koroman was dismissed or removed from service in 1992 or in 1993? Do you know? If not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know that he was removed from this service. There was a dismissal of the chief of the public security station, and later on he was issued a decision appointing him an inspector at the police administration or the security services centre. I know that at one point he was dismissed as the chief of the police station, but I don't think that he was entirely removed from the MUP. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you look at tab 18 now, that is P1457.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Sorry. Are you familiar with this document? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know if I've seen it before. I know of the dismissal of Malko, but this very document didn't reach me at all because in 1993 I was at the administration for police, and I didn't have any other specific duties that would entail my being fully informed about such operative things. But I was aware of the dismissals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you would say that this is not a hand-over pursuant to a regular change in personnel, but rather, the result of some actions against Koroman?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I had no part in this and I can see that this hand-over or this record on hand-over is completely - how shall I put it? - it's not even signed by either the receiving or the handing over party. So it is obvious that this record doesn't reflect the factual or the legal situation which would make it a proper document on hand-over between two executives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV KOVAC
utterances.text: So in my view, this is a completely and utterly incomplete document. And as I said, I did not participate in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you. Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we've reached the point where, although it's a few minutes -- we're a few minutes shy of the 1.45 because of the topics that the Chamber still has to cover, we will reserve that to resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. And we alert the parties and the witness as well that we have made arrangements for an extended session tomorrow. So when we rise at 1.45, we would sit -- we will have an extra session from 2.30 to 4.00. And then it appears inevitable that we will be here on Friday, and we will -- although you had previously indicated that we expected that we would finish by the end of the second session, it was ordinarily the second session at noon on Friday, that we would go through until 1.45. Because it is in everybody's interest that we complete this witness's testimony so he doesn't have to return. So with that, we take the adjournment until tomorrow morning. Before we rise, Mr. Kovac, I would point out to you that having been sworn as a witness, you cannot have any communication with any of the lawyers - apart from your own lawyer who has a peculiar role in this - and should you have any conversation with anybody else outside of the Chamber, you cannot discuss your testimony. So with that, we take the adjournment to continue at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
